$comment: Structured index of user and project preferences. Derived from CLAUDE.md, rules/, and session corrections. Keys are topic slugs; values describe the preference, its source, and priority.

immutability.description: Always create new objects instead of mutating existing ones. Use spread operators, Object.assign, or immutable update utilities. Never modify function arguments in place.
examples: Use { ...obj, field: newValue } instead of obj.field = newValue

test-driven-development.description: Write tests before implementation (RED-GREEN-IMPROVE cycle). Minimum 80% coverage. Use tdd-guide agent proactively for new features.
examples: Write failing test first, then implement to pass
Never skip the RED phase -- confirm the test actually fails before writing code

conventional-commits.description: All commit messages follow Conventional Commits format: <type>: <description>. Types: feat, fix, refactor, docs, test, chore, perf, ci.
examples: fix: prevent XSS in user profile display

small-files.description: Prefer many small files over few large ones. Target 200-400 lines, hard max 800 lines. Functions should be under 50 lines. Organize by feature/domain, not by type.
examples: Extract utility functions into separate modules
Split a 900-line component into feature-focused sub-components

error-handling.description: Handle errors explicitly at every level. Provide user-friendly messages in UI code, detailed context in server logs. Never silently swallow errors.
examples: Wrap async calls in try/catch with specific error types
Return structured error responses from API endpoints

input-validation.description: Validate all inputs at system boundaries using schema-based validation where available. Fail fast with clear error messages. Never trust external data.
examples: Use Zod schemas for API request validation

no-hardcoded-secrets.description: Never hardcode API keys, passwords, tokens, or connection strings in source code. Use environment variables or a secret manager. Rotate any exposed secrets immediately.
examples: Read DATABASE_URL from process.env, not from a config file
Use dotenv for local development only, never commit .env files

parallel-agent-execution.description: Use parallel Task execution for independent operations. Launch multiple agents simultaneously when their work does not depend on each other.
examples: Run security review, test writing, and pattern research in parallel
Use Promise.all for independent async operations
